questions.subject: chemistry
questions.explanation: The longest carbon chain carrying the OH group has four carbons, so the parent is butane. Numbering starts from the end that gives the OH group the lowest locant, which is 2, and the methyl branch then sits on carbon 3. The name is therefore 3-methylbutan-2-ol.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: IUPAC nomenclature of alcohols

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Which alcohol gives an immediate turbidity when shaken with Lucas reagent (concentrated HCl with anhydrous ZnCl2) at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Lucas reagent converts an alcohol into an alkyl chloride, which separates as a cloudy layer. Tertiary alcohols react through a stable carbocation and turn turbid at once. Secondary alcohols take several minutes, and primary alcohols show no turbidity at room temperature.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Chemical reactions of alcohols (classification by Lucas test)

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Propene is treated with diborane (B2H6) in tetrahydrofuran, and the intermediate is then oxidised with alkaline hydrogen peroxide. The major organic product is:
questions.explanation: Hydroboration places boron on the less hindered terminal carbon and hydrogen on the internal carbon, an anti-Markovnikov addition. Alkaline hydrogen peroxide then replaces boron with OH, giving the primary alcohol propan-1-ol. Acid-catalysed hydration of propene gives the Markovnikov product propan-2-ol instead.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Preparation of alcohols from alkenes (hydroboration-oxidation)

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Which of the following is the most acidic compound?
questions.explanation: Phenol loses a proton to form the phenoxide ion, whose negative charge is delocalised into the benzene ring by resonance. Alkoxide ions from ethanol and cyclohexanol have no such stabilisation, and water is itself more acidic than alcohols. The phenoxide route makes phenol the most acidic of these four.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Acidic nature of phenol

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (A) Reimer-Tiemann reaction (B) Kolbe's reaction (C) Williamson synthesis (D) Hydroboration-oxidation of propene. List-II: (I) Propan-1-ol (II) Salicylaldehyde (III) Salicylic acid (IV) Methoxyethane. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Reimer-Tiemann treats phenol with chloroform and NaOH, introducing a CHO group ortho to the OH to give salicylaldehyde. Kolbe's reaction passes CO2 through sodium phenoxide under pressure, giving salicylic acid. Williamson synthesis of sodium methoxide with bromoethane gives methoxyethane, and hydroboration-oxidation of propene gives propan-1-ol.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Preparation of phenols; Reimer-Tiemann and Kolbe reactions; Williamson synthesis

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: 2-Methylbutan-2-ol is heated with excess concentrated sulphuric acid. Which alkene is the major product?
questions.explanation: Dehydration proceeds through a tertiary carbocation formed after protonation and loss of water. Removal of a proton from the neighbouring carbon gives the more substituted, more stable alkene, which is the Saytzeff product. Here that is 2-methylbut-2-ene, the trisubstituted alkene, formed in greater amount than the terminal isomer.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Dehydration of alcohols to alkenes (Saytzeff rule)

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Ethylmagnesium bromide reacts with methanal (formaldehyde), and the product is hydrolysed with dilute acid. The alcohol formed is:
questions.explanation: The ethyl group adds to the carbonyl carbon of methanal, and hydrolysis gives a primary alcohol. Two carbons from the ethyl group and one from formaldehyde give three carbons in total, so the product is CH3CH2CH2OH, propan-1-ol. Propan-2-ol would instead come from methylmagnesium bromide and ethanal.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Preparation of alcohols using Grignard reagents

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Arrange the following in order of increasing acidity: (A) p-Nitrophenol (B) Ethanol (C) Phenol (D) Water.
questions.explanation: Ethanol is the weakest acid of the four, and water is a stronger acid than ethanol because ethoxide is a stronger base than hydroxide. Phenol is far more acidic than water because its phenoxide is resonance stabilised. A para-nitro group withdraws electron density and stabilises the phenoxide further, so p-nitrophenol is the most acidic.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Acidic nature of phenol and effect of substituents

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the dehydration of ethanol with concentrated sulphuric acid. I. At about 443 K, ethene is the major product. II. At about 413 K, diethyl ether is the major product. III. At 443 K, diethyl ether is the major product. Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Ethanol forms an alkyl hydrogen sulphate, which then reacts with a second alcohol molecule at lower temperature to give diethyl ether. At about 443 K, intramolecular dehydration takes over and ethene is the product. Statement III reverses the two temperature outcomes, so it is false.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Dehydration of ethanol to ethene and to diethyl ether

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Phenol is treated with bromine water at room temperature without any catalyst. The major organic product is:
questions.explanation: The OH group strongly activates the ring for electrophilic substitution, so bromine enters at both ortho positions and the para position without a Lewis acid catalyst. The product is 2,4,6-tribromophenol, which separates as a white precipitate and is the classic test for phenol. Bromobenzene would need a catalyst and is not formed here.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Electrophilic substitution reactions of phenol

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: 2-Methyl-2-methoxypropane, (CH3)3C-O-CH3, is treated with one equivalent of cold concentrated HI. Which pair of products is formed?
questions.explanation: Ether cleavage begins with protonation of the ether oxygen. Because one side is tertiary, the C-O bond to the tert-butyl group breaks by an SN1 route, giving the stable tert-butyl cation, which iodide captures. The methyl side remains as methanol, since SN2 attack at a tertiary carbon is not possible.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Reactions of ethers: cleavage by HI

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Consider the following statements about alcohols, phenols and ethers. I. Ethanol boils at a higher temperature than methoxymethane, although both have molecular mass 46. II. Phenol is a stronger acid than ethanol. III. Phenol liberates carbon dioxide from sodium bicarbonate solution. Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Ethanol forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds, which raise its boiling point to about 78 C, while methoxymethane has no O-H group and boils at about -24 C. Phenol is more acidic than ethanol because its phenoxide ion is resonance stabilised. Phenol is too weak an acid to release CO2 from sodium bicarbonate, so statement III is false.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Physical properties of alcohols and phenols; acidic nature of phenol

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Assertion (A): 2-Methylpropan-2-ol is dehydrated more readily than ethanol under the same acidic conditions. Reason (R): The tertiary carbocation formed from 2-methylpropan-2-ol is stabilised by hyperconjugation and by the electron-releasing inductive effect of three alkyl groups.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.explanation: Tertiary alcohols lose water through a carbocation that is stabilised by hyperconjugation and by the inductive effect of three alkyl groups, so milder conditions are enough. Primary alcohols such as ethanol do not pass through a comparably stable cation, which is why they need higher temperatures. The stability of the tertiary cation therefore explains why the tertiary alcohol dehydrates more readily.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Dehydration of alcohols and carbocation stability

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (A) Propan-1-ol with pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) (B) Propan-1-ol with acidified potassium dichromate (C) Propan-2-ol with acidified potassium dichromate (D) Ethanol heated with excess concentrated H2SO4 at about 443 K. List-II: (I) Propanone (II) Propanoic acid (III) Propanal (IV) Ethene. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: PCC stops the oxidation of a primary alcohol at the aldehyde, giving propanal. Acidified dichromate carries a primary alcohol on to the carboxylic acid, propanoic acid. Oxidation of a secondary alcohol gives a ketone, propanone, and hot concentrated acid dehydrates ethanol to ethene.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Oxidation of alcohols (primary, secondary)

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: 1-Methylcyclohexene is treated with diborane in tetrahydrofuran, and the intermediate is oxidised with alkaline hydrogen peroxide. Which is the major product?
questions.explanation: Boron adds to the less substituted alkene carbon, which is the CH carbon, and hydrogen goes to the methyl-bearing carbon, an anti-Markovnikov hydroboration. Oxidation then replaces boron with OH on the same carbon. The product is therefore 2-methylcyclohexan-1-ol, with the OH on the former CH carbon next to the methyl group.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Preparation of alcohols from alkenes (hydroboration-oxidation)

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Methyl tert-butyl ether, (CH3)3C-O-CH3, is to be made by the Williamson synthesis. Which pair of reagents gives the best yield?
questions.explanation: The Williamson synthesis is an SN2 reaction, so the alkyl halide should be methyl or primary. A tertiary alkyl halide undergoes mainly elimination when attacked by a strong base such as an alkoxide. Using tert-butoxide as the nucleophile and iodomethane as the electrophile keeps the bulky group on the alkoxide side and gives the ether.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Preparation of ethers by Williamson synthesis

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: 2-Methylpropene is treated with water in the presence of a dilute acid catalyst. Which alcohol is the major product?
questions.explanation: The acid adds a proton to the terminal CH2 carbon, which leaves the more stable tertiary carbocation as the intermediate. Water then attacks that carbon, and this Markovnikov addition gives 2-methylpropan-2-ol. The anti-Markovnikov primary alcohol is not the major product under acid catalysis.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 7 Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers: Preparation of alcohols by acid-catalysed hydration of alkenes

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Which of the following compounds is optically active?
questions.explanation: A carbon bonded to four different groups is a chiral centre. In 2-chlorobutane, carbon 2 carries H, Cl, CH3 and CH2CH3, so the molecule is chiral and optically active. The other three compounds have no stereocentre.
questions.ncert_ref: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry Part II, Ch 6 Haloalkanes and Haloarenes: Stereochemistry of haloalkanes (chirality)
